story: E005-F005-S001: Implement CLI type definitions and installation infrastructure
story_description: As an onboarding user, I need the app to understand different agentic coding CLIs (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Aider, Cursor, Cody, OpenCode, Amp) with their executable paths, version flags, dependencies, and install commands so that automatic detection and installation can proceed without manual configuration.
task: E005-F005-S001-T001: Create CLITypes.swift with CLI type definitions
task_description: Implement the foundational CLIType enum and supporting types (DependencyType, InstallCommand) in CLITypes.swift. The CLIType enum must define all supported CLI tools with computed properties for displayName, executable, versionFlag, description, isRecommended, dependencies array, and installCommand. This provides the data model for the entire CLI detection and installation subsystem.
atom_description: Create CLITypes.swift containing the CLIType enum with eight cases (claude, codex, gemini, aider, cursor, cody, opencode, amp) and comprehensive computed properties for each. Also define DependencyType enum for runtime prerequisites and InstallCommand enum for installation method variants. This atom is the foundation of the CLI installation service - all detection, installation, and UI components depend on these type definitions.
problem_statement: The onboarding flow needs to detect which agentic coding CLIs are installed and offer to install missing ones. Currently there is no unified model for CLI tools - we need a type-safe enum that captures: (1) the executable name for shell detection, (2) version flag for checking installation, (3) human-readable display name and description, (4) whether the tool is recommended for new users, (5) runtime dependencies like Node.js or Python, and (6) the appropriate install command (npm, pip, brew, etc.). Without this model, detection and installation logic would be scattered and inconsistent across the codebase.

edge_cases: Edge case 1: CLI executable name may differ on some systems (e.g., claude vs claude-code) - executable property returns canonical name
Edge case 2: Install command packages may change versions - use package name without version specifier
Edge case 3: Some tools have multiple installation methods - installCommand returns the primary recommended method
Edge case 4: Decoding unknown CLIType string from JSON should throw DecodingError.dataCorrupted
Edge case 5: InstallCommand associated value strings may contain special characters - ensure proper encoding
Edge case 6: Empty dependencies array is valid for tools with no runtime prerequisites
Edge case 7: Future CLI tools may require additional DependencyType cases - enum is extensible
Edge case 8: shell(script:) case may contain multi-line scripts - String should preserve newlines
failure_modes: FM-001: If executable name is wrong, detection will fail silently - Mitigation: Verify executable names against current CLI documentation before release
FM-002: If install command package name is incorrect, installation will fail - Mitigation: Test installation commands on clean macOS system
FM-003: If InstallCommand Codable implementation has bugs, settings persistence fails - Mitigation: Comprehensive unit tests for encode/decode round-trip
FM-004: If DependencyType is missing a case, certain CLIs cannot express their requirements - Mitigation: Review all CLI documentation for prerequisites
FM-005: If versionFlag is wrong for a CLI, version detection returns error - Mitigation: All major CLIs use --version, verify before adding new ones
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Models/CLITypes.swift file. Remove any imports of CLIType, DependencyType, or InstallCommand from dependent files (should be none if this is the first atom). No data migration required as this is a new type with no persistent storage yet.
